> 1) EU AI Act: We need explicit language on whether your model will be classified as a high-risk system under Annex III for our use case (clinical triage). Please call out any differences between hosted and private deployment options and the compliance controls for each.

Marissa (inline): We will state that for clinical triage used as a decision-support tool, the system can be considered high-risk under Annex III depending on the deployment and claimed autonomy. Our recommended approach:
- Hosted (Redwood Hosted API): provide documented mitigations (traceability, enhanced human oversight, continuous evaluation), and offer a hardened deployment profile that includes stricter monitoring and a certified audit trail. Hosted options are operable in EU regions to satisfy data locality requirements.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-managed deployment reduces some obligations around provider-managed telemetry; we provide the same control surface but allow the customer to retain keys and logs. We will include example clause language that maps to Annex III obligations.

> 2) NIST AI RMF mapping: Can you provide a short table that maps our key risk categories (safety, explainability, data privacy) to specific controls you implement and the artifacts you can supply (e.g., eval reports, test harness, trace logs)?

Marissa (inline): Attached spreadsheet (eval-sampling.xlsx) is populated with the mapping and suggested artifacts. High-level examples:
- Safety -> continuous regression tests, adversarial prompt suite, safety filter logs -> Artifact: regression reports (.pdf), test harness code snippet, sample failing prompts.
- Explainability -> structured output options, attribution tooling, model card metadata -> Artifact: model card, structured response schema.
- Data privacy -> optional request-side encryption, data retention settings, redaction hooks -> Artifact: retention policy doc, audit logs.

> 3) Regression cadence: We need a proposed baseline post-deployment regression schedule and how regressions are detected/triaged. Specifically: sampling sizes, metrics to monitor, and rollback criteria.

Marissa (inline): Proposed baseline:
- Regression cadence: weekly automated sampling (n=1,000 prompts) + monthly manual evaluation (n=5,000 prompts) for first 90 days, then weekly sampling + quarterly manual review.
- Metrics: generation quality (BLEU/ROUGE where applicable), hallucination rate (domain-specific heuristics), safety filter trigger rate, latency percentiles, and semantic drift score.
- Detection & triage: automated alerting on metric thresholds or statistically significant drops; triage by CS/ML ops with three-tier severity (P0/P1/P2) and canary rollback to previous model version if P0.
